concepts.why: The patient presented with sudden vision loss and optic disc swelling, and imaging studies showed focal enhancement along the enlarged right optic nerve, which is consistent with a glioma of the optic nerve.

The patient developed sudden vision loss and was found to have no light perception vision, with marked swelling of the optic disc and occlusion of the superior branch artery, which is consistent with a central retinal artery occlusion.
The patient presented with peripapillary retinal hemorrhages, which is a common finding in retinal vein occlusion.

The vitreous biopsy showed a hypercellular sample with astrocytic neoplasm, and immunohistochemistry was positive for glial fibrillary acid protein, oligodendrocyte transcription factor 2, mutant IDH-1 protein, and p53.
The patient presented with blurred vision and a relative afferent pupillary defect, which is consistent with optic neuritis.
The patient developed sudden vision loss and was found to have marked swelling of the optic disc, which is consistent with ischemic optic neuropathy.
The patient presented with peripapillary retinal hemorrhages and occlusion of the superior branch artery, which is consistent with retinal ischemia.
The patient presented with peripapillary retinal hemorrhages, which is a common finding in vitreous hemorrhage.
